title: Footnotes Gone Feral
blurb: The parts of history your textbook skipped because nobody would believe them.

cards.say: Martin Van Buren [was the first president born a citizen of the United States], [gave us the word OK, which started out as his nickname], [grew up speaking Dutch as his first language], and [was the last sitting vice president elected president until 1988].
cards.real: OK first appeared in an 1839 Boston newspaper as a joke for oll korrect. His 1840 campaign's OK Clubs, for Old Kinderhook, made it popular.

cards.say: James Garfield [gave part of a campaign speech in German], [worked the mules on a canal boat as a teenager], [won his party's nomination on the 36th ballot], and [published his own proof of the Pythagorean theorem while president].
cards.real: His trapezoid proof was published in 1876, while he was a congressman from Ohio, five years before he became president.

cards.say: Chester A. Arthur [was born in Canada and moved to Vermont as a baby], [helped throw his college's bell into the Erie Canal], [helped win a case that desegregated a New York streetcar line], and [sold 24 wagonloads of White House furniture at auction].
cards.real: Arthur was born in Vermont in 1829. Claims that he was really born in Canada were just a rumor.

cards.say: Grover Cleveland [got married inside the White House], [had secret surgery on a yacht while the public thought he was fishing], [was mayor of New York City before becoming president], and [vetoed more bills in his first term than all earlier presidents combined].
cards.real: Cleveland was mayor of Buffalo in 1882 and then governor of New York, before winning the presidency in 1884.
src: https://potus.com/grover-cleveland (414 vetoes in his first term, against 204 by all earlier presidents)

cards.say: Rutherford B. Hayes [got America's first Siamese cat as a gift from the King of Siam], [had the first White House telephone, and its number was 1], [took his first oath of office privately inside the White House], and [started the White House Easter Egg Roll after Congress banned it at the Capitol].
cards.real: Siam the cat came in 1878 from David Sickels, an American diplomat at the consulate in Bangkok, not from the king.

cards.say: Dwight D. Eisenhower [was named David Dwight at birth], [was born in a small town in Kansas], [never saw combat in 35 years as a soldier], and [got squirrels banished for digging up his White House putting green].
cards.real: Eisenhower was born in Denison, Texas, in 1890. His family moved back to Kansas before he was two, and that's where he grew up.
src: https://www.history.com/articles/10-things-you-may-not-know-about-dwight-d-eisenhower (trapped and released in Rock Creek Park)

cards.say: Emperor Norton [demanded a bridge across San Francisco Bay decades before one was built], [paid for meals with money he printed himself], [pardoned the police officer who arrested him], and [later added Protector of Canada to his royal title].
cards.real: His add-on title was Protector of Mexico, taken up in the 1860s. He had declared himself Emperor of the United States in 1859.

cards.say: Arthur Conan Doyle [believed two girls' fake fairy photos were real], [worked as a ship's surgeon on an Arctic whaling voyage], [was knighted for creating Sherlock Holmes], and [helped make skiing popular in England].
cards.real: Doyle was knighted in 1902 for his writing defending Britain's side in the Boer War, not for Sherlock Holmes.

cards.say: Julia Child [was turned away by the Army for being too tall], [published her first cookbook at 29], [helped cook up a shark repellent for a US spy agency], and [voiced a character in a 1993 animated dinosaur movie].
cards.real: Mastering the Art of French Cooking, her first book, came out in 1961, when she was in her late forties.

cards.say: The Pig War [started when a British farmer shot an American's pig], [had a pig as its only casualty], [left US and British troops sharing one island for about 12 years], and [was settled by the German Kaiser in 1872].
cards.real: It was the other way around: American Lyman Cutlar shot a pig belonging to Britain's Hudson's Bay Company in June 1859.

cards.say: The Hope Diamond [was stolen with the French crown jewels in 1792], [keeps glowing red after an ultraviolet light is switched off], [was dug out of a South African mine in the 1800s], and [was sent to the Smithsonian by registered mail in a brown paper box].
cards.real: It came from India, likely the Kollur Mine, and reached Europe in the 1600s, when Louis XIV bought it as the French Blue.

cards.say: Big Ben [is the name of the bell, not the clock or the tower], [rings for a clock kept on time with old pennies on its pendulum], [cracked soon after it was hung and went silent for four years], and [hangs in a tower renamed for the Queen's 1953 coronation].
cards.real: The Clock Tower was renamed Elizabeth Tower in 2012 for Queen Elizabeth II's Diamond Jubilee, her 60th year on the throne.
